seoTitle: Crucible — a native Plex client for iPhone, built on Linux
metaDescription: Crucible is a fast, native Plex client for iPhone with a Resume-first Home, offline downloads, Skip Intro, Picture-in-Picture, a Year-in-Review dashboard, and Liquid Glass design — open source and built entirely on Arch Linux without Xcode.
heroHeadline: Your Plex library, done right on iPhone
heroSubhead: A fast, native Plex client with a Resume-first Home, offline downloads, Skip Intro, Picture-in-Picture, and a Year in Review of your viewing — open source and built entirely on Arch Linux without ever opening Xcode.
highlights: A Resume-first Home, filter chips, and posters that let the artwork lead
Offline downloads: season sheet, keep-next-episodes, Live Activity
Skip Intro your way, Picture-in-Picture, and background audio
Open source under GPL-3.0 — one dependency, GRDB, for the stats store

features.title: A player that respects your time
features.body: Skip Intro and Skip Credits from Plex markers — as a button with a live progress sweep, automatic with Undo, or off. Picture-in-Picture, background audio, and lock-screen controls come along, and credits roll the next episode automatically.

features.title: Take it offline
features.body: Download movies, whole seasons, or single episodes at the quality you pick — from Original down to Data Saver. A season sheet downloads all, unwatched, or the next three episodes and can keep the next ones downloaded as you watch. Downloads keep running in the background, auto-resume, and stay Wi-Fi-only unless you say otherwise, with a storage summary and one-tap cleanup of watched titles. A Live Activity tracks progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island — a WidgetKit extension compiled and signed entirely on Arch Linux via xtool.

features.title: Plays anything
features.body: Direct play when your device handles the file natively, automatic HLS transcoding through Plex's universal transcoder when it doesn't.

features.title: Browse the way you think
features.body: Home opens on a Resume hero, then Continue Watching, Up Next, your week in watch time, and Recently Added. Library grids have filter chips for Unwatched and In Progress, genre and sort, an A–Z scrubber, and raw folder browsing. Search groups results by type with a Top Result.

features.title: Discover more
features.body: Cast and crew, More Like This recommendations, subtitle and audio track selection, and adjustable playback speed on every title.

features.title: Know your viewing
features.body: The You tab shows your server and connection status, Watch History grouped by day, and a Year-in-Review dashboard — watch time, streaks, an activity heatmap, top shows, and a shareable card built from your own Plex history.

features.title: Continues across devices
features.body: Watch progress syncs to your server, resume picks up where you left off, and Handoff plus Spotlight carry titles between your devices.

features.title: Built different
features.body: Swift 6 and programmatic UIKit with Liquid Glass on iOS 26, Light and Dark, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver throughout. Cross-compiled on Arch Linux and deployed over USB. No Xcode, no macOS, one dependency.

howItWorks.body: Authenticate with Plex over OAuth. Crucible discovers your servers and picks the best reachable connection automatically.
Pick up with the Resume hero, filter your poster grids, or search across everything you own.
Direct play or transcode, skip the intro, send it to Picture-in-Picture, and let Up Next roll the next episode.

faq.q: Is Crucible on the App Store?
faq.a: No. Crucible is a free, open-source personal project, not an App Store release. You build it once with xtool and sign it with your own Apple ID; the steps above take about fifteen minutes, and a free Apple ID is enough. GitHub releases carry the changelog, not an installable app.

faq.q: Do I need a Mac or Xcode to build it?
faq.a: No. Crucible is written in Swift 6 and programmatic UIKit and built with SwiftPM and xtool, which runs on Linux, Windows (WSL) and macOS and installs to an iPhone over USB. Building it on Linux without a Mac is exactly how it is made.

faq.q: How long does a free Apple ID build last?
faq.a: Seven days. After that the app stops opening until you install it again: plug the phone in and run `./scripts/install-ios.sh` once more. A paid Apple Developer account lasts a year.

faq.q: What does it need to run?
faq.a: An iPhone on iOS 17 or later and a Plex Media Server you can reach. Crucible talks directly to your server, so a phone away from home needs a route to it; it works well over Tailscale.

faq.q: Does it support Skip Intro, PiP, and lock-screen controls?
faq.a: Yes. Skip Intro and Skip Credits come from Plex chapter markers, Picture-in-Picture and background audio keep playback going, and the lock screen and Control Center drive play, skip, scrub, and next episode.

faq.q: Can I download movies and shows to watch offline?
faq.a: Yes. Download movies, full seasons, or single episodes at the quality you choose — Original, High, Medium, Low, or Data Saver. Downloads run in the background and resume after interruptions, stay Wi-Fi-only unless you allow cellular, and live in a dedicated Downloads tab with a storage summary, the live queue, and one-tap cleanup of watched titles. A season sheet downloads all, unwatched, or the next three episodes, and can keep the next ones downloaded as you watch. A Live Activity shows live progress on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, and a notification fires when a download finishes while you're away. Offline playback uses the same player, so Skip Intro/Credits, resume, PiP, background audio, and lock-screen controls all work with no network.
Yes — GPL-3.0, with one third-party dependency (GRDB, for the statistics store) and pure Apple frameworks for everything else. Read the code, file an issue, or fork it on GitHub.

install.title: Put it on your iPhone,
install.intro: Crucible isn't on the App Store. You build it once with xtool, signed with your own Apple ID, and it installs over USB. A free Apple ID is enough. You need an iPhone on iOS 17 or later, a cable, and a Mac, a Linux PC, or Windows with WSL.

steps.title: Install xtool
steps.body: xtool builds and installs iOS apps without Xcode's interface. On a Mac, install Xcode 26 or newer from the App Store, open it once, then install xtool.
steps.note: On Linux or Windows (WSL) you install Swift 6.4, usbmuxd, and Xcode's `.xip` from Apple instead; the step-by-step guide below lists each command.

steps.title: Sign in to Apple
steps.body: Pick `1: Password` to use any Apple ID, a free one included, then enter the two-factor code. Your credentials go only to Apple. On Linux and Windows it also asks for the path to the `.xip`.

steps.title: Build it and put it on your phone
steps.body: Plug the phone in, unlock it and tap Trust. The script checks your setup, builds Crucible in release mode and installs it. The first build takes several minutes. If it asks for Developer Mode, turn it on in Settings > Privacy & Security, restart the phone and run the script again.

steps.title: Trust it and open it
steps.body: On the phone: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management > your Apple ID > Trust, then open Crucible and sign in with Plex. A free Apple ID's build stops opening after 7 days; run the script again to renew it.
